name: Community Choices Waiver — Self-Directed Attendant Care
summary: The Community Choices Waiver helps South Carolina adults who need nursing-home level care stay at home. Its self-directed Attendant Care service (scope effective July 1, 2025) lets the participant hire, schedule and supervise their own attendant, who may be a qualified family member. A fiscal intermediary contracted by SCDHHS pays the attendant.
who_qualifies: Age 65+, or age 18–64 with a physical disability.
Meets nursing-facility level of care through a Community Long Term Care (CLTC) assessment.
Meets South Carolina Medicaid financial rules.
The participant or an appointed employer of record can supervise the attendant, as certified by the USC nurse.

who_can_be_paid.adult_children_relatives: yes — attendants may be related to the participant within the South Carolina Family Caregiver Policy.
who_can_be_paid.spouse: limited — the scope bars any 'legally responsible adult' (a person legally required to use their own assets for the participant's care); spouses are not named either way, so confirm with your case manager.
who_can_be_paid.parent_of_minor: no — Community Choices serves adults; children use the MCC Waiver.

pay.detail: SCDHHS pays self-directed attendants through a contracted fiscal intermediary in one-hour units; the current hourly attendant rate for Community Choices is not published in the scope of services.

hours_or_budget: The case manager authorizes hours in the service plan. If assessed need exceeds 40 hours a week, a second attendant must be found for the extra hours.

waitlist.detail: Community Choices has a set number of slots; a waiting list forms when they are full.

self_directed_or_agency: Either. In self-directed attendant care the participant or employer of record supervises the attendant and a fiscal intermediary pays them; agency personal care is also offered.
how_to_apply: Call SCDHHS Healthy Connections at 888-549-0820 or submit a CLTC referral online (phoenix.scdhhs.gov/cltc_referrals/new).
Complete the CLTC nursing-facility level-of-care assessment and the Medicaid financial application.
Once on the waiver, ask your case manager for self-directed Attendant Care.
The attendant completes TB screening, background check, Medicaid provider enrollment and EVV/billing training before the first authorization.

contacts.name: SCDHHS Healthy Connections Member Contact Center

faqs.q: Can I get paid to care for my parent on the Community Choices Waiver?
faqs.a: Yes, through self-directed Attendant Care. The participant can hire a qualified family member as the attendant, and SCDHHS's fiscal intermediary pays them.

faqs.q: Can a spouse be the paid attendant?
faqs.a: It is unclear. The state's scope bars any legally responsible adult but does not name spouses. Ask your CLTC case manager before counting on it.

faqs.q: How many hours can one attendant work?
faqs.a: The state tries to keep each attendant at 40 hours a week or less. If more care is needed, a second attendant covers the extra hours.

faqs.q: What does an attendant need before starting?
faqs.a: Be 18 or older, pass background checks, have TB screening, enroll as a Medicaid provider and attend EVV and billing training at the SCDHHS area office.

faqs.q: How much does an attendant earn?
faqs.a: SCDHHS does not publish a current hourly figure for this service. Ask your case manager.

name: Medically Complex Children (MCC) Waiver — Children's Attendant Care
summary: The MCC Waiver serves South Carolina children with serious, long-lasting medical conditions who need hospital level of care. Since July 1, 2025, its self-directed Children's Attendant Care option pays eligible parents, relatives or guardians $16.20 an hour to give the extra hands-on care their child needs. Morning Sun Financial Services enrolls caregivers and pays them by direct deposit.
who_qualifies: Enrolled in the MCC Waiver: meets hospital level of care with a chronic condition expected to last more than 12 months.
Age 1 through 21 for Children's Attendant Care.
Needs hands-on help with at least two of seven activities of daily living beyond what a parent normally gives a child the same age.

who_can_be_paid.adult_children_relatives: yes — qualified relatives can be approved as paid children's attendant caregivers.
who_can_be_paid.spouse: n/a — the participant is a child.
who_can_be_paid.parent_of_minor: yes — the FAQ says families may hire qualified family members, including a parent of a minor child.
who_can_be_paid.live_together: optional — care is clocked at home (or to and from Medicaid services) via a phone app.

pay.detail: SCDHHS's Children's Attendant Care FAQ (rev. Aug. 11, 2025) sets the 2025 rate at $16.20 per hour, paid by Morning Sun Financial Services about twice a month.

hours_or_budget: The MCC waiver nurse case manager assigns minutes and hours to each extraordinary-care task. Each caregiver can work no more than 40 hours a week; extra approved hours go to a second caregiver or an agency aide.

waitlist.detail: Not published on the SCDHHS page; MCC is a capped waiver.

self_directed_or_agency: Self-directed: the family manages the caregiver; Morning Sun is the fiscal agent and a USC nurse handles training and approval.
how_to_apply: If your child is not on the MCC Waiver, call Healthy Connections at 888-549-0820 or submit a referral at phoenix.scdhhs.gov/cltc_referrals/new.
Once enrolled, ask your waiver nurse case manager for Children's Attendant Care.
Pass the background check and CPR/First Aid training (at your own cost) with help from the USC nurse.
Complete the Morning Sun enrollment packet and use the time-tracking app to clock in and out.

contacts.name: SCDHHS Healthy Connections Member Contact Center

faqs.q: Can I get paid to care for my medically complex child in South Carolina?
faqs.a: Yes. Since July 1, 2025, parents of children on the MCC Waiver can be paid as Children's Attendant Caregivers if the child needs extraordinary hands-on care.

faqs.q: How much do parents get paid?
faqs.a: As of 2025 the rate is $16.20 an hour, paid by direct deposit about twice a month.

faqs.q: How many hours can I be paid for?
faqs.a: Up to 40 hours a week per caregiver. If your child is approved for more, another relative or an agency aide covers the rest.

faqs.q: Can I be paid while my child is at school or in the hospital?
faqs.a: No. You can only clock in when you and your child are home, or while taking your child to and from a Medicaid-covered service.
SCDHHS tells caregivers to ask a tax expert. Morning Sun can help with tax forms at (855) 767-4871.

faqs.q: Do I have to give up my agency aide?
faqs.a: No. Children's Attendant Care is optional, and you can mix it with an agency aide for remaining hours.
